ownership_reason: Only the gold parses the base URI and resolves the link; hop 1 answers a missing attribute with "" and hands on the node's base URI and the attribute value, and hops 2-4 pass them on as they stand (their javadoc: the link, as written in the attribute). The gold promises to make the link absolute by reading it relative to the base URI, which http://jsoup.org/path/?foo is not for the query-only link ?foo against http://jsoup.org/path/file?bar. The path of the base URL is known only inside the gold (parsing a URL throws a checked MalformedURLException that no plumbing hop declares or catches); stripping the base's query, prefixing the whole base URI or a "./" upstream all leave java.net.URL reading the link against the directory /path/. The convention is pinned outside the gold: StringUtil.resolve(URL, String) gives a link starting with "?" the base URL's path before java.net.URL reads it (its comment: java resolves '//path/file + ?foo' to '//path/?foo', not '//path/file?foo' as desired), StringUtil.resolve(String, String) is its String entry point and HttpConnection.Response.execute resolves redirect locations with it; Node.absUrl's javadoc says the value is treated as a URL relative to the element's baseUri and made absolute using that; StringUtilTest resolvesRelativeUrls pins the sibling resolver's adjustments of java.net.URL, and NodeTest absHandlesDotFromIndex, handlesBaseUri and ElementTest testRelativeUrls pass through the chain.
